newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short rates come off highs, bonds steady.
newsitem.headline: Greek short rates come off highs, bonds steady.

text.p: Greek short-term depos and forex forwards came off intraday highs to trade around 12 percent in late dealings, bonds were stable at lower prices and ecu/drachma remained rangebound, dealers said.
"Short-term interbank rates have come off intraday highs to trade around 12 percent in periods up to a month," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank. "The overnight rate hit 13.10 percent today."
Dealers attributed the softer interbank rates to rising liquidity but remained too high.
Bonds were stable at lower prices with FRNs little changed, delaers said.

"The bond market has calmed down after prices of fixed rate bonds suffered losses of 30 basis points in early dealings," said a bond trader at a private bank. "The outlook for the FRN auction is not good right now."
The finance ministry is going to auction 150 billion drachams of seven-year floaters on June 26.
Ecu/drachma was sitting tight in the 309.15/33 range and traders said higher interbank rates were inducing forex inflows.

"Ecu/drachma is trading around 309.15/20 right now. The high of the day was 309.33," said a senior forex dealer at a foreign bank. "High interbank rates have prompted some players to sell ecus for drachmas."
The dealer said about 50 million ecus for drachmas were sold at today's fixing.
The mark was quoted at 157.76/86 from Monday's 157.880 fix, the dollar at 271.63/73 drachmas from 272.520 and the ecu at 309.11/21 from 309.250 drachmas.
